## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Chattamāṇavakavimānavatthu* ("The Boy Chatta’s Mansion", Vv 53) is a narrative discourse in the *Vimānavatthu* collection of the Pali canon. The text recounts how the Buddha instructs a young boy named Chatta on taking refuge and observing the moral precepts. In secondary scholarship on Buddhist death practices and rebirth ideology, Gregory Schopen cites story no. 53 of the *Vimānavatthu* as an instance illustrating the prominent belief in early Pali literature that an individual's mental state or disposition at the moment of death strongly determines their future fate and rebirth [Schopen 1978].

**Sources**

- [Schopen 1978] Gregory Schopen, The Bhaiṣajyaguru-sūtra and the Buddhism of Gilgit (1978) — Discussion of Vv 53 illustrating the determination of rebirth by the mental state at death.
